record_body:
Account summary
- BlueHeron Payer Services (enterprise payer services org). Exploring Redwood for regulated LLM inference supporting PHI-adjacent workflows.
- Primary motion: Healthcare ABM pilot. Strong pull for Private/VPC deployment; Dedicated considered as interim if contract + security gating for Private takes longer.

Current status (Procurement)
- In procurement/legal review. They have a defined vendor onboarding path and are pushing hard on DPA/BAA, liability, audit rights, and data retention.
- They asked explicitly: “If any PHI is processed, will you sign a BAA?” and “Can we ensure prompts/outputs are not stored beyond configured retention / not used for training?”

Stakeholder map (known)
- Procurement (process owner): Vendor Management lead + category manager (names redacted in notes; procurement prefers all comms via portal + email).
- Legal: Commercial counsel + privacy counsel (driving DPA + BAA decision).
- Security/GRC: Security assurance manager + GRC analyst (questionnaire, SOC2 evidence, audit logging expectations).
- Platform/Infra: Director of Platform Engineering (owns VPC networking, key mgmt, SIEM ingestion, runtime ops expectations).
- Data/Analytics: Applied ML lead (evaluation criteria; cares about throughput and cost predictability).

Use-case + technical requirements (from discovery + follow-ups)
- Initial use cases they are prioritizing:
  - Prior auth / claims notes summarization (structured outputs; consistent formatting)
  - Member support agent assist (streaming chat; low latency)
  - Provider communication review (classification + summarization)
- Performance targets (rough):
  - P95 latency: < 800ms to first token for agent-assist prompts; < 3.5s total for typical summarizations (1–2 pages)
  - Throughput: expecting spikes during business hours; wants predictable capacity vs noisy neighbors
- Deployment preference:
  - Private in their cloud VPC is “strongly preferred” for PHI-adjacent workloads.
  - Needs VPC connectivity (peering / private link) and documented network boundary.
- Data handling constraints:
  - Wants configurable retention controls and clarity on what is logged vs stored.
  - Requires audit logging export to their SIEM (format + fields) and a clear list of what Redwood can/can’t see.
- Key management:
  - KMS integration required; they asked about customer-managed keys and key rotation responsibilities.

Procurement / contracting steps (their stated process)
1) Vendor onboarding + security intake
   - Complete security questionnaire; attach SOC 2 report under NDA; provide security overview + reference architecture.
2) Contract package
   - MSA (BlueHeron paper), DPA exhibit, Security addendum, SLA exhibit.
   - If PHI: BAA addendum required (they treat as gating for any PHI processing, even in Private/VPC).
3) Insurance + compliance artifacts
   - COI, subprocessors list, incident response summary, vulnerability mgmt summary.
4) Technical POC approval
   - They will allow a time-boxed POC once legal has an acceptable DPA + (if applicable) BAA posture.

Key open legal questions (tracked)
- BAA applicability:
  - They want a clear statement: whether Redwood will sign a BAA, under what deployment mode(s), and what workloads qualify.
  - They asked if “Private/VPC means you are a subcontractor handling PHI” and whether Redwood personnel access can be restricted.
- DPA scope:
  - Data processing roles (controller/processor), cross-border transfers, and subprocessors.
  - Data retention: confirmation of retention configuration + deletion timelines.
- Training / data use:
  - They require explicit contractual language that customer data is not used to train models.
- Audit logs:
  - They want audit log export details in an exhibit (fields: user access, admin actions, config changes, request metadata; with PHI-safe boundaries).

Security review notes (high-level)
- Asked for: SOC2 Type II, pen test summary, incident response policy excerpt, and “evidence of audit logging + retention controls.”
- Noted they will accept a staged approach if controls are documented (start with non-PHI prompts for POC; move to PHI after BAA + controls verified).

Recent activity timeline
- 2026-01-29: Internal align (Diego + Fatima) that this is a Private-first account; Dedicated only as bridge if procurement drags.
- 2026-02-06: Fireflies call (Procurement/legal process) — ff_2026-02-06_blueheron_procurement_process
  - Procurement outlined required documents, portal workflow, and realistic cycle time (4–8 weeks once redlines start).
  - Legal flagged BAA as non-negotiable if PHI is in scope.
- 2026-02-10: Sent Healthcare Security FAQ addendum + Private/VPC reference architecture (links in record).
- 2026-02-14: Platform team follow-up: requested written responsibility matrix for Private/VPC ops (patching, monitoring, key rotation, log shipping).

Deal strategy / guidance
- Position Private/VPC as primary path for PHI-adjacent workloads, with clear boundaries and customer-controlled networking.
- Propose a two-phase evaluation:
  - Phase 1 (no PHI): Validate latency/cost, structured output stability, SIEM log export, and KMS integration plan.
  - Phase 2 (PHI): Conditional on BAA/DPA closure and evidence sharing under NDA.

Next steps (owner + dates)
- Diego: schedule joint call with BlueHeron legal + procurement to walk through DPA/BAA posture and reduce back-and-forth (target week of 2026-02-17).
- Fatima: deliver a one-pager “Private/VPC shared responsibility” + answers on KMS integration options (customer-managed keys, rotation, access controls).
- Olga/Aisha: confirm what evidence can be shared under NDA (SOC2 report distribution, pen test summary) and provide approved language for audit logging + retention exhibits.

Internal notes
- High intent account; procurement is strict but process-driven.
- If we can answer BAA + data handling cleanly, this is likely a meaningful Private opportunity in Q2. If BAA stance is unclear, risk of stall/lose to hyperscaler “in their tenant” offerings.
